title: Exceptional fibres and conormal bundles of regular surface point blowups
statement: Let $X$ be an integral regular Noetherian scheme of dimension $2$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Let $p\in X$ be closed, put $d=\dim\mathcal O_{X,p}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and let $b:X'=\operatorname{Bl}_pX\to X$ be the blowup of the reduced closed point [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Put $E=b^{-1}(p)$, with its scheme-theoretic fibre structure and closed immersion $i:E\hookrightarrow X'$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-closed-immersion], and $k=\kappa(p)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Then $d\in\{1,2\}$. If $d=1$, then $b$ is an isomorphism and $E\cong\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If $d=2$, then $E$ is an integral regular Noetherian scheme of dimension $1$, proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], and an effective Cartier divisor in $X'$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. There is a $k$-isomorphism $r:E\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf P^1_k$ such that $\mathcal C_{E/X'}\cong r^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_k}(1)$ as invertible $\mathcal O_E$-modules [def-sc-p1-standard, def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. Here, for the ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ of $i$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $\mathcal C_{E/X'}=i^*\mathcal I$ is the conormal sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-functorial].

source.place: Tag 0AGQ (resolve-lemma-blowup), especially (1) and (3), globalized at the closed centre by localization. The dimension-one case is the invertible-centre case of the blowup universal property (cor-nagata-blowup-cartier-iso); the projective-line regularity, dimension and properness are the standard two polynomial charts and projective-space structure.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $p$, with corresponding maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $A=\mathcal O_{X,p}=R_{\mathfrak n}$. Integrality makes $R$ a domain. Prime chains in $R_{\mathfrak n}$ give chains of irreducible closed subsets of $X$ by taking their closures, so $d\le\dim X=2$. If $d=0$, the prime $(0)$ in the domain $R$ equals $\mathfrak n$, hence $p$ is the generic point of $V$ and of $X$. Its being closed would force the integral scheme $X$ to have just one point, contradicting dimension $2$. Thus $d\in\{1,2\}$. Write $\mathcal J$ for the ideal of the reduced closed point; its stalk at $p$ is the maximal ideal of $A$, and its stalk at every other point is the whole local ring.

source.place: Tag 0AGQ (lemma-blowup), localization setup; elementary dimension-chain reduction for the global statement.

proof.text: On each member of an affine covering with Noetherian coordinate rings, the ideal defining $\mathcal J$ is finitely generated, by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Its associated ideal sheaf is quasi-coherent by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and consequently coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. In particular $\mathcal J$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, as required by the blowup principalization theorem below.

source.place: Tag 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian), applied to the closed-point ideal on a locally Noetherian scheme.

proof.text: If $d=1$, regularity means that $\mathfrak m_A=(x)$ for one element $x$. The domain $A$ has dimension one, so $x\ne0$, and multiplication by $x$ identifies $A$ with $\mathcal J_p$. At every other point $\mathcal J$ has stalk equal to the local ring. Hence every stalk of this coherent ideal is free of rank one. Apply [lem-sc-coherent-free-stalks-locally-free]; its local free ranks are one, as seen on these stalks. Thus $\mathcal J$ is invertible, and [cor-nagata-blowup-cartier-iso] makes $b$ an isomorphism. Its scheme-theoretic fibre over $p$ is therefore $\operatorname{Spec}k$, by the fibre-product definition of a fibre.

source.place: Tag 0807 (lemma-blow-up-effective-Cartier-divisor); coherent local freeness as in algebra.tex Tag 0GWM.

proof.text:
Assume now $d=2$. Use the affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ above and $T=R\setminus\mathfrak n$. The map $g:\operatorname{Spec}A	o V	o X$ is flat. Indeed, a prime of $A=R_{\mathfrak n}$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak n$ of $R$; its stalk map is $R_{\mathfrak q}	o (R_{\mathfrak n})_{\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak n}}$, an isomorphism by the fraction descriptions in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]: its inverse sends $(a/s)/(b/u)$ to $au/(sb)$, where $s,u
otin\mathfrak n$ and $b
otin\mathfrak q$, so $sb
otin\mathfrak q$. Thus these stalk maps are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], as required by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The ideal $\mathcal J$ extends to $\mathfrak m_A$. Apply the comparison constructed in [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] and its isomorphism assertion [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change]. This identifies $Y=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m_A}\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A	imes_X X'$. Denote its projection by $h:Y	o X'$. Taking the further fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ identifies $F=Y	imes_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}k$ canonically with $E$, with the same $k$-structure. On every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $b^{-1}(V)$, the corresponding open of $Y$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(T^{-1}C)$.

source.place: Tag 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up), followed by associativity of fibre products.

proof.text:
Choose generators $x,y$ of $\mathfrak m_A$, using regularity and $d=2$. Both $(x,y)$ and $(y,x)$ are regular sequences by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. First identify $Y$ with the affine blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m_A}(\operatorname{Spec}A)=\operatorname{Proj}\mathcal R_A(\mathfrak m_A)$: for the one-member affine cover $\{\operatorname{Spec}A\}$ the glue datum of [def-nagata-global-blowup-glue-data] consists of the single local model $\mathsf B_{\operatorname{Spec}A}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m_A}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ of [def-nagata-global-blowup-local-model], and [prop-nagata-global-blowup-cover-independent] identifies the global blowup over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with it. By [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] the $x$- and $y$-charts then cover $Y$; [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart] identifies their maps [def-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-map] with the standard opens $D_+(xu)$ and $D_+(yu)$ of the Rees Proj, where $u$ is its degree-one bookkeeping variable. Their rings, by [lem-trf-blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation], are
$$C_x=A[t]/(xt-y),\qquad C_y=A[s]/(ys-x),$$
where $t=y/x$ and $s=x/y$. By [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal], the ideal $\mathfrak m_A\mathcal O_Y$ is $(x)$ and $(y)$ on these charts. Consequently the fibre charts are $C_x/(x)=k[t]$ and $C_y/(y)=k[s]$. On the intersection, $t$ is invertible and $s=t^{-1}$: the intersection is the standard open where the other degree-one generator of the Rees algebra is invertible relative to the chosen generator, equivalently $D(t)$ on the $x$-chart. Thus these fibre charts glue precisely to the two charts of [def-sc-p1-standard]. They give a $k$-isomorphism $r:E=F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf P^1_k$.

source.place: Tag 0AGQ (lemma-blowup), proof of (1), using the explicit charts of more-algebra.tex Tag 0BIQ (lemma-blowup-regular-sequence).

proof.text:
By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], $\mathcal I=\mathcal J\mathcal O_{X'}$ is an invertible ideal defining an effective Cartier divisor. This divisor is exactly the scheme-theoretic fibre $E$, since the reduced closed point has ideal $\mathcal J$: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $b^{-1}(V)$ the fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_R R/\mathfrak n)=\operatorname{Spec}(C/\mathfrak nC)$, with $\mathfrak nC=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}C,\mathcal J\mathcal O_{X'})$ and $R/\mathfrak n=R_{\mathfrak n}/\mathfrak nR_{\mathfrak n}=k$ as $\mathfrak n$ is maximal, while over $X\setminus\{p\}$ the fibre is empty and $\mathcal J\mathcal O_{X'}$ is the unit ideal. We also need its conormal on the localized model $Y$. The conormal map of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-functorial] for $h$ identifies the original conormal on $E$ with that on $F$. Indeed, on an affine open with ideal $I\subset C$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-conormal-sections] writes this map as
$$I/I^2\longrightarrow (T^{-1}I)/(T^{-1}I)^2,\qquad a\bmod I^2\longmapsto a/1\bmod (T^{-1}I)^2.$$
Here $(T^{-1}I)^2=T^{-1}(I^2)$: a product $(a/t)(b/u)$ has numerator $ab\in I^2$, and a fraction $ab/t$ equals $(a/t)(b/1)$, with finite sums giving both inclusions. After restriction to $E$, every element of $T$ is already a unit (its nonzero residue in $k$ is invertible). Thus its inverse sends $a/t$ to $t^{-1}a$ in $I/I^2$. This is well-defined: equality of localized representatives means that an element of $T$ kills their cross-multiplied difference modulo $I^2$, and multiplication by that element is invertible on the $C/I$-module $I/I^2$. The two composites are identities. The formulas commute with restriction of fractions, so agree on overlaps and identify the conormal sheaves on all of $E$.

source.place: Tag 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor); morphisms.tex Tags 01R3 (lemma-affine-conormal) and 01R4 (lemma-conormal-functorial), with the displayed elementary localization calculation.

proof.text: On $\operatorname{Spec}C_x$ the element $x$ is a nonzerodivisor: $C_x=A[\mathfrak m_A/x]\subset A_x$ by [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], and $A$ is a domain. Likewise $y$ is a nonzerodivisor on the other chart. Hence the conormal modules given by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-conormal-sections] are $(x)/(x^2)\cong k[t]$ with basis $[x]$, and $(y)/(y^2)\cong k[s]$ with basis $[y]$. Explicitly $\bar a\mapsto ax\bmod x^2$ is bijective because $x$ is a nonzerodivisor, and similarly for $y$. On the overlap $[y]=t[x]$, since $y=tx$ already in the ambient chart. In [def-sc-p1-standard], the frames $g_0,g_1$ of $\mathcal O(1)$ satisfy $g_1=tg_0$. Sending $r^*g_0$ to $[x]$ and $r^*g_1$ to $[y]$ therefore glues to an isomorphism $r^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal C_{E/X'}$. The two displayed free rank-one modules also verify invertibility directly.

source.place: Tag 0AGQ (lemma-blowup), (3), and divisors.tex Tag 0B3P (lemma-conormal-effective-Cartier-divisor); explicit transition calculation.

proof.text: Finally [lem-sc-p1-regular-dimension-one] gives Noetherianity, regularity and dimension one for $\mathbf P^1_k$, and [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] gives its properness over $k$, taking the two-element index set and base $\operatorname{Spec}k$. It is integral: its two standard affine charts have domain rings $k[t]$ and $k[s]$, are reduced, and have common nonempty dense open $\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$. Each chart is irreducible, and the density of their common open makes their union irreducible; the union is also reduced and nonempty. The equivalence in [def-pc-integral-scheme] proves integrality. All these properties pass along the $k$-isomorphism $r$ to $E$, completing the $d=2$ case.
